customer_interviews.what: Talking to users one-on-one to learn how they actually behave and what they struggle with, without leading them to the answer you want.

subskills.name: Interview guides & non-leading questions
subskills.example: Ask 'tell me about the last time you did X', never 'would you use Y?'

subskills.name: Recruiting participants
subskills.example: A screener that filters for people who did the task in the last 30 days.

subskills.name: Synthesis & affinity mapping
subskills.example: Tag 20 transcripts, cluster into 5 themes, and rank by frequency.

subskills.name: Sharing findings
subskills.example: A 10-minute readout with three clips that make the point for you.

ladder.associate: Takes notes in interviews and can run one from a guide.
ladder.mid: Plans and runs interview rounds; synthesizes into decisions.
ladder.senior: Designs research programs for big bets; teaches others to interview.
ladder.lead: Ensures continuous discovery is funded and practiced across teams.

build: Read: 'The Mom Test' (short) and 'Continuous Discovery Habits'.
Project: interview 8 people about a problem, synthesize themes, write a one-page readout.
At work: join every customer call you can; offer to run the next round.
signals: Ran 45 customer interviews across 3 segments; findings changed the Q2 roadmap.
Built a reusable screener and interview guide adopted by the whole product org.

user_research.what: The broader toolkit for learning about users: qualitative and quantitative methods, when each fits, and how to run them rigorously.

subskills.name: Choosing the right method
subskills.example: Use interviews to find the problem, a survey to size it, a usability test to check the fix.

subskills.name: Usability studies
subskills.example: Five moderated sessions; measure task success and where people stall.

subskills.name: Contextual & field research
subskills.example: Spend a day on the warehouse floor watching the tool get used.

subskills.name: Research ops & partnership
subskills.example: Scope the question with the researcher; own the decision the research informs.

ladder.associate: Participates in studies and reads research reports critically.
ladder.mid: Scopes and runs lightweight studies; partners well with UXR on bigger ones.
ladder.senior: Builds a research plan for a product area; chooses methods deliberately.
ladder.lead: Invests in research capacity and holds teams to evidence-based decisions.

build: Course: an HCI or UX research methods course (many universities' intro courses are online).
Project: run a diary study with 5 people for a week and write it up.
At work: pair with a researcher on a study from plan to readout.
signals: Led a mixed-methods study (12 interviews, 600-response survey) that defined the SMB segment.
Ran monthly usability studies; task success on core flows rose from 62% to 88%.

discovery.what: Finding out which problems are worth solving and whether a proposed solution works, before committing engineering time.

subskills.name: Opportunity mapping
subskills.example: Map the outcome to the opportunities under it and the solutions for each.

subskills.name: Assumption & hypothesis testing
subskills.example: List the riskiest assumption and design the cheapest test for it.

subskills.name: Cheap tests: fake doors, concierge, prototypes
subskills.example: Add a 'Export to Notion' button and count clicks before building it.

subskills.name: Jobs-to-be-done framing
subskills.example: 'When I close the month, I want to find discrepancies fast, so I can sign off by day 3.'

ladder.associate: Runs small validation tests designed by others; documents results.
ladder.mid: Owns discovery for a feature: opportunities, assumptions, tests.
ladder.senior: Runs discovery for a product area and kills bets early based on evidence.
ladder.lead: Makes discovery a standard practice; funds exploration before commitment.

build: Read: 'Continuous Discovery Habits' (Torres); 'Testing Business Ideas' for a catalogue of tests.
Project: pick an idea, write its riskiest assumptions, run one cheap test, report.
At work: propose a fake-door or prototype test before the next big build.
signals: Ran 6 fake-door tests in a quarter; killed 4 ideas and shipped the 2 with real demand.
Built an opportunity-solution tree that became the team's planning backbone.

personas_jtbd.what: Describing who you are building for in a way that is specific enough to change decisions: segments, personas, and the jobs they hire the product for.

subskills.name: Segmentation
subskills.example: Split users by company size and workflow, not by demographics.

subskills.name: Evidence-based personas
subskills.example: Personas built from 20 interviews and usage data, each with a real quote.

subskills.name: Ideal customer profile
subskills.example: Define the ICP narrowly enough that sales knows who to skip.

ladder.associate: Knows the product's personas and uses them in specs.
ladder.mid: Builds or refreshes personas from research for a feature area.
ladder.senior: Defines segments and ICP for a product; aligns GTM on it.
ladder.lead: Decides which segments the company serves and which it won't.

build: Exercise: write two contrasting personas for an app you use, with the different job each hires it for.
Course: any product-marketing or GTM class covering segmentation and ICP.
At work: audit whether the current personas are backed by data; propose fixes.
signals: Redefined the ICP to mid-market ops teams; win rate in that segment rose 30%.
Built 4 research-backed personas used across product, design, and marketing.

surveys_feedback.what: Collecting feedback at scale and turning it into something the team can act on: surveys, NPS, beta programs, and in-product feedback loops.

subskills.name: Survey design
subskills.example: Ten questions max, one open-ended, no double-barrelled questions.

subskills.name: NPS / CSAT programs
subskills.example: Track NPS by segment and read the verbatims, not just the number.

subskills.name: Beta & early-access programs
subskills.example: Fifteen design partners who get builds early and a weekly call.

subskills.name: Feedback triage & loops
subskills.example: Tag every request, report monthly, and tell requesters when it ships.

ladder.associate: Runs small surveys and triages feedback into the backlog.
ladder.mid: Owns a beta program or feedback channel for a product area.
ladder.senior: Designs feedback systems used across the product; reads signal from noise.
ladder.lead: Ensures customer feedback reaches planning at the org level.

build: Course: a short survey-design module (question wording, bias, sampling).
Project: run a survey of 50 people on a topic, analyze, and present three findings.
At work: start a feedback triage ritual and a 'you asked, we shipped' note.
signals: Ran a 15-customer design partner program that shaped the v2 launch.
Built a feedback tagging system; top-10 requests reviewed monthly with leadership.

metrics_kpis.what: Choosing the few numbers that tell you whether the product is working, instrumenting them, and watching them with discipline.

subskills.name: Defining metrics
subskills.example: Define 'active' precisely (did a core action in 7 days) and write it down.

subskills.name: Instrumentation & tracking plans
subskills.example: A tracking plan listing every event, its properties, and who owns it.

subskills.name: Dashboards & reporting
subskills.example: One dashboard per team with 5 metrics, reviewed every Monday.

subskills.name: Metric trees & funnels
subskills.example: Break revenue into traffic × conversion × AOV and know which you move.

ladder.associate: Reports on existing metrics and keeps a dashboard current.
ladder.mid: Defines success metrics for features and gets them instrumented.
ladder.senior: Owns the metric tree for an area; spots and explains movements fast.
ladder.lead: Sets the company-level metrics and the review cadence around them.

build: Course: a product analytics course (Amplitude and Mixpanel both publish free ones).
Project: write a tracking plan and metric tree for an app you know.
At work: own the weekly metrics review for your team for a quarter.
signals: Defined the activation metric now used company-wide and instrumented it end to end.
Built the funnel dashboard that surfaced a 20% drop-off at address entry.

data_driven.what: Using data to make and defend decisions: pulling it, questioning it, and knowing when it is wrong or insufficient.

subskills.name: Hands-on analysis
subskills.example: Pull the cohort retention curve yourself before the meeting.

subskills.name: Data skepticism & quality
subskills.example: Check whether the spike is real or a logging change.

subskills.name: Turning insight into decisions
subskills.example: Every analysis ends with a decision and an owner.

subskills.name: Combining qualitative & quantitative
subskills.example: Use the data to find the where, interviews to find the why.

ladder.associate: Reads dashboards and asks for the right cuts of data.
ladder.mid: Does their own analysis in SQL or a BI tool; makes decisions from it.
ladder.senior: Finds non-obvious insights and changes strategy with them.
ladder.lead: Builds a data-informed culture; invests in instrumentation and analytics.

build: Course: an intro data analysis course that includes real datasets (SQL + spreadsheets).
Project: analyze a public dataset and write a one-page memo with a recommendation.
At work: answer one question a week with data you pulled yourself.
signals: Analyzed 2 years of churn data; identified the onboarding gap behind 40% of losses.
Built a self-serve cohort dashboard that cut data requests to analysts by half.

ab_testing.what: Running controlled experiments to learn whether a change actually causes the outcome you want, and reading the results honestly.

subskills.name: Hypothesis design
subskills.example: 'Shortening signup to 2 fields will raise completion by 5pts' with the reasoning.

subskills.name: Primary metrics & guardrails
subskills.example: One primary metric, two guardrails (latency, support tickets).

subskills.name: Sample size, power & duration
subskills.example: Compute the MDE before launch; commit to two full weekly cycles.

subskills.name: Reading results & significance
subskills.example: Don't stop at day 3 because it's green; watch for novelty effects.

subskills.name: Experiment platforms & rollouts
subskills.example: Bucket by account not user for B2B tests; keep a long-term holdout.

subskills.name: Experiment reviews & learning
subskills.example: A searchable log of every test, result, and decision.

ladder.associate: Sets up tests on a platform with a template; reports results.
ladder.mid: Designs experiments end to end: hypothesis, metrics, sizing, readout, decision.
ladder.senior: Runs an experimentation program for an area; catches bad tests and bad reads.
ladder.lead: Builds the platform and culture: velocity, rigor, and what not to test.

build: Course: a statistics-for-experimentation module (Udacity's A/B testing course is free; 'Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments' is the reference).
Project: design a full test plan for a change in an app you use, including sample size math.
At work: ship one experiment with a pre-registered hypothesis and a written readout.
signals: Ran 22 experiments in 2024 with a 35% win rate; documented every readout.
Introduced guardrail metrics and a minimum run length after two false positives shipped.

statistics.what: Enough statistics to size experiments, forecast, read a regression, and know when a number is noise.

subskills.name: Distributions & descriptive stats
subskills.example: Report p50 and p90 latency, never just the mean.

subskills.name: Inference & hypothesis tests
subskills.example: Know what a 95% interval does and doesn't say.

subskills.name: Forecasting & modelling
subskills.example: Build a simple driver-based forecast with best, base, and worst cases.

subskills.name: Causal thinking
subskills.example: Use a pre/post with a control region when you can't randomize.

ladder.associate: Reads averages and rates correctly; knows what a sample is.
ladder.mid: Sizes tests, reads intervals, builds simple forecasts.
ladder.senior: Spots confounds and bad inference; models scenarios for decisions.
ladder.lead: Partners with data science on methodology; sets standards for rigor.

build: Course: an intro statistics course with applied exercises (Khan Academy or a university MOOC).
Book: 'Naked Statistics' for intuition; 'Statistical Rethinking' if you want depth.
At work: build the forecast model for your area's next planning cycle.
signals: Built the driver-based forecast used for 2025 planning; within 6% of actuals.
Caught a Simpson's-paradox read on a test that would have shipped a regression.

financial_analysis.what: Modelling the money: costs, revenue, margins, and budgets, well enough to make a business case and read a P&L.

subskills.name: Unit economics
subskills.example: Know the cost to serve a customer and what moves it.

subskills.name: Financial models
subskills.example: A three-scenario model with the two assumptions that matter most exposed.

subskills.name: Budgets & cost management
subskills.example: Track cloud cost per active user monthly and own the trend.

subskills.name: Reading a P&L
subskills.example: Explain how your feature shows up in revenue, cost, or margin.

ladder.associate: Reads a budget and can do a basic cost/benefit.
ladder.mid: Builds a business case model for a feature.
ladder.senior: Owns the financial model for a product; forecasts revenue and cost.
ladder.lead: Owns a P&L or budget; trades investments across products.

build: Course: a 'finance for non-finance managers' or intro corporate finance class.
Project: build a unit-economics model for a subscription product with public numbers.
At work: sit with finance for a planning cycle and build the model for your area.
signals: Built the pricing model that projected $4M ARR from the new tier; actuals $4.6M.
Cut infra cost per request 30% by modelling and renegotiating the storage tier.
